newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk bonds parade into market.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk bonds parade into market.

text.p: Corporate bond secondary trading activity took a backseat on Thursday, paving the way for a parade of new junk deals, players said.
"The focus in the high-yield sector today was centered around new issues, specifically, TransaAerica's deal," said one high-yield player.
TransAmerica Energy Corp's sold more than $1.5 billion (principal amount) in new junk bonds which players said were met with very good reception by investors.
The bond's prices rose soon after the issues were priced, suggesting strong demand, they said.
The company's $475 million in 11-1/2 percent senior secured notes due 2002 were quoted 102-1/2 bid, 102-3/4 offer after pricing at par.
Its $1.13 billion (principal amount) of 13 percent zero coupon bonds due 2002 traded as high as 79 bid, but were most recently quoted at 78, after pricing at 77.6779, one trader said.
Jefferies & Co Inc was the sole manager of the junk bond offering from TransAmerican, a holding company owned by oil and gas mogul John Stanley.
Another high-yield issuer was Synder Oil Corp, an oil and gas exploration and production company, which sold $175 million in 10-year 144A notes at 8.875 percent.
NationsBanc Securities Inc managerd the deal, sources said.
"These deals went very well and quickly traded up in the aftermarket," one player said of the above deals.
Snyder's 8-3/4 paper was quoted at a 99-3/4 bid, 100-1/4 offer, at the close.
Intercel Inc also tapped the market with $300 million in 10-year 144A notes to yield 11-1/8 percent, sources said.
In the broader high-yield market, prices ended the day 1/8 to 1/4 higher in moderate trading, players said.
"There was a good tone in the market today ... we saw some moderate trade with everyone looking to be buyers," said another high-yield player.

Among issues performing well were Nextel Communications' 11-1/2 percent bonds which were quoted higher at an 88-1/2 bid, on news that the company's digital wireless network was seeing rapid user growth, exceeding analyst expectations.

The company's president and chief operating officer, Timothy Donahue, speaking at a PaineWebber technology conference here, said the success of Nextel's business oriented digital network leads him to believe that the company will turn cash flow positive ahead of schedule.
Nextel's other paper traded at a 79 bid, 79-1/2 offer.
Flagstar senior paper also traded higher to a 101 bid, they said.
In the supermarket sector, Grand Union paper gained two points to trade at 78-1/2 bid, traders said. Penn Traffic debt was quoted 52 bid, 53 offer, they said.
U.S. high-grade secondary corporate trade endured another dull session on Thursday with spreads remaining unchanged to Treasuries as player await Friday's key U.S. jobs report.
"People are just squaring away positions ahead of tomorrow's numbers ... it's been really quiet," said one high-grade trader.
On Friday, the Labor Department is scheduled to release U.S. payrolls/unemployment figures for May.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economist forecast a 5.0 percent unemployment rate and an increase of 219,000 in payrolls.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
